LESSON: CULTURE AND SOCIAL ORGANISATION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.3: Culture and Social organisation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Culture and Social organisation, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six General.

Key inquiry question: How would we preserve positive aspects of African traditional culture?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. describe age-groups and age-sets in African traditional society,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Culture and Social organisation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. explain the functions of a clan in traditional African society,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Culture and Social organisation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. identify aspects of African traditional culture that ought to be preserved,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Culture and Social organisation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. desire to uphold aspects of African traditional culture that ought to be preserved. Learner is guided to: ● brainstorm features of age groups and age-sets and share in class, learners with speech difficulties could use alternative modes of communication to share their responses, ● discuss the functions of a clan in traditional African society, ● create posters on aspects of African traditional culture that ought to be preserved, learners with manipulation difficulties could use appropriate assistive technology or adapted drawing/ writing resources to develop the posters. They could also give instructions as a peer; learner support assistant or teacher develops the posters, How would we preserve positive aspects of African traditional culture? 21 ● sing, hum, tap, clap or nod to the rhythm of songs on aspects of African traditional culture that ought to be preserved.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Culture and Social organisation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. desire to uphold aspects of African traditional culture that ought to be preserved. They could also give instructions as a peer; learner support assistant or teacher develops the posters, How would we preserve positive aspects of African traditional culture? 21 ● sing, hum, tap, clap or nod to the rhythm of songs on aspects of African traditional culture that ought to be preserved.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Culture and Social organisation together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Communication and Collaboration: Learners brainstorm the meaning of age-groups and age-sets and share in class.

 Creativity and Imagination: Learners create posters on aspects of African traditional culture that ought to be preserved.
